notes: Page 2 is a generic introduction (open the box, sort the bricks) with no building steps, so no pieces or joins were added.
Page 3, step 1: white 2x8 plate is the base (first piece, rests on nothing).
Step 2: red 2x4 studded wheel arch is placed on one end of the plate. Its bottom clutches the plate.
Page 4, step 3: a red 1x4 plate has a red 1x1 plate added, then the 1x4 is placed on the studs of the red wheel arch (b2).
The callout shows only one 1x1 plate, on the left end of the 1x4. The parts box says 2x, so I put the second 1x1 on the other end of the 1x4. This is a guess.
I assumed the 1x4 plate rests only on the wheel arch and not on the white base plate.
Page 5, step 4: two more red wheel arches are added next to the first, so three arches sit in a row.
The three arches are 12 studs long but the white base plate is only 8 long, so the arches must be staggered or overlapping. The picture does not show clearly which pieces each new arch clutches.
I assumed b6 rests on the white plate (b1) and the red 1x4 plate (b3), and b7 rests on the white plate (b1).
Page 6, step 5: three black 2x2 wheel-holder plates are placed on the three red arches. A dark green 1x2 plate goes between the first and second holder.
I assumed b8 sits on b2, b9 on b6 and b10 on b7. The picture does not show which arch is leftmost.
I assumed the green 1x2 plate (b11) rests on b2 and b6, the two arches it sits between.
Page 7, step 6: the model is flipped over. A white 1x2 plate is pressed onto two red studs at the end of the model.
I assumed those two studs belong to the end arch, b7, so b12 rests on b7. The picture does not show which arch it is.
Page 8, step 7: a dark green 1x2 plate and a black 2x2 towball-socket plate are added at the end of the model, side by side.

The picture does not show exactly which pieces each one clutches. I assumed the green plate rests on the end arch (b7) and the white 1x2 plate (b12), which it appears to cover. I assumed the black socket plate rests on b7.
Page 9, step 8: two gold side-handle 1x2 plates and two gold 1x1 plates go on either side of the green and black pieces at the end of the model.
The pieces look tan or gold in the picture. I took them as Pearl Gold from the parts list, which has 2x lego-48336 and 6x Pearl Gold 1x1 plates.
I assumed all four pieces rest on the end arch (b7). The picture does not show which pieces each one clutches.
Page 10, step 9: a red 4x4 plate covers the white base plate and the red arch studs on the open end of the model.
I assumed it rests on the white plate (b1), the arches b2 and b6, and the red 1x4 plate (b3). The picture does not show exactly which pieces it clutches.
Page 11, step 10: a red 2x4 plate and a red 1x4 plate cover the green, black and gold pieces next to the red 4x4 plate. The gold handles and the black socket stay visible.
The picture does not show exactly which pieces each plate clutches. I assumed the 2x4 (b20) rests on b13, b14 and b7. I assumed the 1x4 (b21) rests on b7 and the 4x4 plate (b19).
Page 12, step 11: a white 2x3 plate goes on the red 4x4 plate (b19), on the end away from the gold handles.
I assumed it rests only on b19, because the picture does not show it overlapping the 2x4 plate.

Page 13, step 12: four red clip tiles are pressed onto the red 4x4 plate (b19) around the white 2x3 plate, at its corners. Four plain red 1x1 grooved tiles go on the studs of the white 2x3 plate (b22).
The picture shows only one tile being added by arrow, but the parts box says 4x. I assumed the four tiles go on four of the six white studs.
The clip tiles are placed on the 4x4 plate. I did not add clip joins because no bars are involved yet.
Page 14, step 13: this is a separate sub-assembly, the locomotive front, and is not yet attached to the main model.

Step 1 is a red bracket (b31). Step 2 puts a black inverted bracket (b32) on its face, with a clear round tile at each upper corner and black round plates at the lower corners. Step 3 adds two black grille slopes (b39, b40) and another black round plate, shown by the arrow.

The picture does not show exactly which stud each small piece sits on. I assumed the four black round plates and both clear tiles are on the red bracket, and the grille slopes are on the black bracket. Ports are left null where unclear.
The output schema has no rests_on field, so stacking is given as joined edges. Pages 3 to 13 gave their stacking in notes only. They have no edges yet.
Page 15: the front sub-assembly from page 14 (red bracket b31 with grille and lamps) is pushed onto the front end of the main body. No new pieces.
The picture does not show which stud it clutches. I assumed the bracket's 1x2 plate clutches the exposed front studs of the white base plate (b1).
Page 16, step 14: a white 2x3 plate goes on the rear plates, and two dark green 1x4 grooved tiles go side by side on the red 4x4 plate (the boiler top).
I assumed the white plate (b41) rests on the red 2x4 (b20) and red 1x4 (b21) plates, and both green tiles rest on the red 4x4 plate (b19).

The clip tiles and 1x1 tiles from page 13 are not visible in this view. I assumed they are on the side not shown, or are meant to be replaced here, and I did not remove them from the graph. This is unclear.

Page 17, step 15: this is built 2x. Each copy is a small stack on the white 2x3 plate (b41): white round plate, red round plate (step 1), pearl gold round plate, then white round brick on top (step 2). They form the two chimney or dome stacks.
I identified the four pieces in the parts box as white 6141, red 6141, pearl gold 6141 and white 3062b. The box shows them as white, red and tan or gold round plates plus a taller white round brick.
The picture does not show exactly which studs of b41 the two stacks use. I assumed stud.1.1 for the first and stud.2.3 for the second.
Page 18, step 16: built 2x. Each copy is a red 1x2x2 window with a clear glass pane inserted, placed on the white 2x3 plate (b41) next to the chimney stacks.
The picture does not show which studs of b41 are used. The two stacks use stud.1.1 and stud.2.3, so I assumed the windows use stud.2.1/2.2 and stud.1.2/1.3 to fill the six studs.
Page 19, step 17: two gold 4L bars (handrails) are clipped along the two sides of the boiler.

Each bar is held by the two red clip tiles from page 13 on its side and by one gold side-handle plate. I assumed b23 and b24 are on one side and b25 and b26 on the other. The picture does not show which clip tile is on which side.
I used clip.1 of each side-handle plate (b15, b16).
Page 20 starts a new sub-model, the tender or coal car. The locomotive from pages 3 to 19 is finished.
Step 1: two red 2x2 round bricks with axle hole are stacked (b46, b47).
Step 2: a red inverted bracket 1x2 - 1x2 (b48) and a red 1x2 plate (b49) go on the top round brick. The bracket sits on one pair of studs and the plate goes on the other pair.
The bracket piece in the parts box is hard to identify. I took it as the red lego-99780 from the parts list.
Page 21, step 3: a red round 2x2 plate with axle hole (b50) goes on the red bracket (b48) and red 1x2 plate (b49).

Step 4: a dark green round 2x2 plate with axle hole (b51) goes on b50, then a white round 2x2 jumper plate with centre stud (b52) goes on top. The white piece is taken as lego-18674 from the parts list, since it is the only white round 2x2 plate there.

Page 22, step 5: a reddish-brown round piece goes on the white jumper plate (b52), then a clear round 1x1 tile goes on top. I took the brown piece as the reddish-brown lego-3941 round 2x2 brick, which is the only reddish-brown piece it can be. It looks flatter in the picture.

Step 6: a black wheel-holder plate (b55) is pushed up onto the underside of the bottom red round brick (b46). I took it as lego-4600, since the other black 2x2 pieces in the parts list look different. The picture is small, so this is a guess.
The clear tile might also be 3062b-based. I used lego-98138 Trans-Clear, which has 3 in the parts list.
Page 23: step 7 turns the round tower assembly on its side. Step 18 of the main model fits it onto the locomotive as the boiler, with its black plate (b55) pressed onto the body. No new pieces.
I assumed the black plate clutches the open studs of the red 4x4 plate (b19). The picture is small and does not show which plate it clutches.

Page 24, step 19: a red 4x4 plate goes on top as the cab roof. It sits on the two red windows (cab1.win, cab2.win) and the two white round bricks at the tops of the chimney stacks (stack1.top, stack2.top).
The model is also turned upright on this page. This adds no pieces.
Page 25, step 20: two dark green curved 2x4 bricks (b57, b58) are placed side by side on the red 4x4 roof plate (b56) to make the curved cab roof.

Page 26, step 21: this builds the chimney. A red round open-stud brick goes on a red jumper plate, a tan cone goes on top with its bar in the open stud, and white ice cream scoops (the smoke) go on the cone. The chimney is then pressed onto the front of the boiler.

The small tan piece in step 2 looks like a short cap. I identified it as the tan lego-11610 ice cream cone, the only tan round part in the parts list that fits. The scoops have no catalogue ports, so their joint to the cone's stud has no port.
I assumed the chimney's jumper plate clutches the two black studs of the black wheel-holder plate (b55) visible on the boiler front. The picture does not show this clearly.

Page 27, step 22: six black wheels are fitted to the wheel holders of the three black 2x2 wheel-holder plates (b8, b9, b10) under the locomotive, two wheels per plate. The red arrow shows one wheel going on.
The wheels are modelled as turning freely (revolute), clipped into the wheel holders. The wheel-to-holder port pairing is by convention, since the catalogue has no pin port for the wheel.
Page 28 starts a new sub-model, a green and red car (the coal or gift wagon). The locomotive is finished.

Step 1: a white plate (b69) is the base. The picture of this plate shows about 6 studs per row, so I took it as lego-3795 (2x6). The parts list has 2x 3795 white but only 1x 3034 white, and the 3034 was used for the locomotive base on page 3.
Step 2: a red 2x4 wheel arch (b70) goes on one end of the base plate.
Page 29, step 3: a dark green 2x4 plate (b71) and a second red wheel arch (b72) are added, so the two arches sit at the ends with the green plate between them.
Step 4: the model is flipped, and two red 1x2 plates (b73, b74) go on the studs of the green plate in the middle.
I assumed the green plate sits on the white base plate (b69) and touches both arches. The picture does not show the exact stacking.
Page 30, step 5: a black 2x2 towball-socket plate (b75) and two gold 1x1 plates (b76, b77) go on the end arch (b72). The gold plates sit on either side of the socket plate.
The gold plates look tan or gold in the picture. I took them as Pearl Gold from the parts list.
I assumed all three pieces rest on b72 only. The picture does not show exactly which studs they use.

Page 31, step 6: a black 1x4 towball plate (b80) goes on the arch (b70) at the open end of the model. Two red 1x4 plates (b78, b79) go on the red arch studs next to the white plate. The arrows show them on the studs beside the white plate.
The picture does not show exactly which studs each piece uses. I assumed b78 and b80 rest on b70 and b79 rests on b72.

Page 32, step 7: two red 1x6 plates and two red 1x2 plates are added along the long sides of the model. Only one 1x6 is shown with arrows, but the parts box says 2x. I assumed the second 1x6 and the 1x2 plates go on the opposite side or in the gaps.

The arrows on the 1x6 plate point to the black towball plate end (b80) and the gold plate (b76) at the other end. So b81 rests on b80, b76 and the red 1x4 plate b78. The mirror side b82 rests on b77, b79 and b72.
The two 1x2 plates (b83, b84) are placed on the arches b70 and b72 as a guess. The picture does not show them clearly.
Page 33, step 8: two white 1x2 plates and four white round 1x1 plates are placed on the red 1x6 side plates at the ends of the model, to look like a white trim.
I assumed one 1x2 plate and two round plates on each side. The first side is on b81 and the second on b82. The picture does not show exactly which studs each uses.

Page 34, step 9: two red 1x2x1 panels go on the white 1x2 plates (b85, b86), and four red round plates go on the four white round plates (b87 to b90). One round plate is shown by an arrow and the parts box says 4x.
I assumed each panel is on its own white 1x2 plate and each red round plate is on its own white round plate. The pairing of round plates is a guess.
Page 35, step 10: four gold round plates go on the four red round plates at the corners. Two dark green curved 1x4 bricks lie in the wagon bed.
I assumed each curved brick sits on one of the red 1x4 plates (b78, b79). The picture does not show which studs they clutch.
Page 36, step 11: the model is flipped. Two black wheel-holder plates with two wheels each are built, and one is pressed onto each wheel arch, b70 and b72, on the underside.
I assumed b103 goes on b70 and b104 on b72. The picture does not label which arch is which.

Page 37, step 12: two small gift boxes are built. The lime box is a lime plate, a black plate and a lime tile. The orange box is an orange plate, a black plate and an orange tile (the ribbon is the black layer).
Step 1 shows the lime plate with the black plate, step 2 shows both finished boxes. The lime box is shown placed between the green curved bricks in the wagon bed.
The picture shows only the lime box placed. I assumed the orange one goes in the same bed. I put the lime box on b73 and the orange box on b74, the two red 1x2 plates in the bed.

Page 38, step 13: this builds a candy cane. Six round 1x1 plates are stacked from the bottom up as red, green, white, red, green, white. A red curved brick (the hook) goes on the white plate at the top, and a red 1x1 tile goes on the stud at the end of the hook.
Steps 1 and 2 build the stack, and step 3 adds the hook and tile.
The catalogue lists no stud on the curved brick lego-6091, but the picture shows the tile pressed onto its end. I joined the tile to the curved brick with no port named.
Page 39: the candy cane from page 38 is pressed onto a free stud in the wagon bed, next to the lime gift. No new pieces.
I assumed it clutches the free stud of the red 1x2 plate b74. The orange gift is not visible in this view, so its position is still uncertain.

Page 40, step 14: two sweets are added. First, a pink swirl round plate goes on a lavender flower plate, and the flower goes on a free stud in the wagon bed. Second, a white round tile with a red spiral print goes on the stud of a white signal paddle, which makes a lollipop leaning on the wagon side.
The parts box shows a beige tile. I took it as the white lego-98138pr0013 spiral tile, because it is the one in the picture with a spiral and the catalogue has no other spiral tile.
I assumed the flower goes on the free stud of b73. The lollipop's stick rests against the wagon side next to the panel b92, so I used a contact edge. The picture does not show it clipped to anything.

Page 41, step 15: an ice cream cone with a chocolate scoop and two cookies are added to the wagon bed. The cone is a tan cone with a reddish-brown swirl plate on top. The cookies are the two cookie-print round tiles.

The parts list has only one lego-11610 tan cone, and I used it for the chimney on page 26 (b61). On page 26 the small tan piece may actually have been a Pearl Gold round plate. If so, b61 should be a lego-6141 Pearl Gold plate and the chimney scoops should sit on it. This page uses the cone for the ice cream, so the chimney part on page 26 is probably wrong.
The picture does not show exactly where the cone and cookies sit, so I used contact edges to the green curved bricks (b101, b102) instead of studs.
Page 42: the wagon is coupled to the locomotive. The towball on the wagon's black 1x4 plate (b80) snaps into the towball socket plate at the rear of the locomotive (b14). No new pieces.

Page 43 starts a new sub-model, the passenger car. Step 1: a white 2x8 plate (b131) is the base. The picture shows 8 studs per row, so I used lego-3034, the only 2x8 white plate in the parts list. The list has only one, and I used it for the locomotive base (b1) on page 3. That earlier plate was probably the lego-3795 2x6, so b1 may be the wrong type.
Step 2: two dark green 1x2 plates (b132, b133) go across the two ends of the base plate.
Page 44, step 3: a dark green 2x4 plate (b134) goes in the middle of the base plate, and two red wheel arches (b135, b136) go either side of it. The arches sit at the ends of the car.
I assumed each arch rests on the base plate, the green 2x4 plate and its own end green 1x2 plate. The picture does not show exact studs.

Page 45, step 4: the model is flipped, and two red 1x2 plates (b137, b138) go on the exposed studs of the dark green 2x4 plate (b134) in the middle. Only one is shown with arrows, but the parts box says 2x.

Page 46, step 5: a black towball-socket plate (b142) goes on the arch at one end. Two red 1x6 plates (b140, b141) go along the two long sides, one per side, and a red 1x2 plate (b139) goes at the other end. Only one 1x6 is shown with arrows, but the parts box says 2x.

The picture does not show exactly which studs each piece uses. I assumed the socket plate rests on b136, the 1x2 plate on b135, and each 1x6 plate on both arches and one of the red 1x2 plates (b137, b138).
Page 47, step 6: a black 1x4 towball plate (b143) goes on the end of the model opposite the socket plate. It sits across the end arch (b135) and the red 1x2 plate (b139).

Page 48, step 7: two red 1x2 plates (b144, b145) go on the exposed studs of the end arch (b136) beside the black socket plate (b142), one on each side. No arrows are shown. I assumed they rest on the end arch b136.

Page 49, step 8: this is built 2x. A gold 1x1 plate is pushed onto the underside of one end of a red 1x8 plate. Each 1x8 plate is then placed along one side of the car, over the red 1x6 plate and the red 1x2 plate on that side.

I assumed b146 sits on b140 and b144, and b147 sits on b141 and b145. The gold plates only hold the end of each 1x8, so they are joined only to their 1x8 plate. The picture does not show what else they touch.

Page 50, step 9: two gold lattice fences and two dark green 1x2 bricks go on the red 1x8 side plates. There is one fence and one brick on each side, with the brick at the other end of the plate from the fence.
I assumed b150 and b152 sit on b146, and b151 and b153 sit on b147. The picture does not show the exact studs.

Page 51, step 10: built 4x. Each copy is a small post of three round plates, white at the bottom, then red, then pearl gold on top. The four posts go at the four corners of the car's rim, on the red 1x8 side plates (b146, b147).
The picture does not show which stud each post uses. I assumed the end studs of each 1x8: stud 1 and stud 8 of b146, then stud 1 and stud 8 of b147.
Page 52, step 11: two clear 1x2 bricks (windows) go on the green 1x2 bricks, one per side. Four white round bricks cap the four corner posts built on page 51.
I assumed b154 sits on b152 and b155 on b153. Each round brick sits on the gold plate of one post, post1 to post4, in order. The picture does not show which post is which.
Page 53, step 12: two dark green 1x2 plates go on top of the clear 1x2 bricks (b154, b155), one per side.
Page 54, step 13: built 4x. Each copy is a red 1x2x2 window with a clear glass pane. Two windows go on each long side of the car, on the red 1x8 plates (b146, b147), between the corner posts.
The picture does not show exactly which studs of the 1x8 plates they use. I assumed studs 3 and 4 and studs 5 and 6 on each plate.
Page 55, step 14: two red 2x6 plates (b162, b163) make the roof, one over each long side. Each rests on its side's two windows and two white round bricks.

I assumed b162 covers the b146 side (windows pwin1 and pwin2, round bricks b156 and b157) and b163 covers the b147 side (windows pwin3 and pwin4, round bricks b158 and b159). This follows how I numbered the pieces on pages 51 to 54.
Page 56, step 15: a red 2x4 plate goes across the middle of the roof. Two white 1x2 plates and two dark green 1x2 plates go on the roof ends, giving the roof a raised lantern layout.

The picture does not show which plates sit where. I assumed the 2x4 spans both roof plates (b162, b163), and each white and green 1x2 plate rests on one of the roof plates: b165 and b167 on b162, b166 and b168 on b163.

Page 57, step 16: the car is flipped. Two black wheel-holder plates with two wheels each are built, and one is pressed onto each wheel arch, b135 and b136, on the underside. This is the same step as page 36.
I assumed b169 goes on b135 and b170 on b136.

Page 58, step 17: the car is turned upright. Four dark green curved 2x2 bricks make the curved roof, two at the ends and two in the middle. The picture shows the two end bricks already on and two arrows for the middle ones, which makes four in total.

The picture does not show exactly which studs each brick uses. I assumed b175 and b176 sit on the roof plates and green 1x2 plates at the ends (b162/b167, b163/b168), and b177 and b178 sit on the roof plates and white 1x2 plates in the middle (b162/b165, b163/b166).
Page 59, step 18: a red 2x2 brick (b179) goes on the roof, with two clear 1x2 plates (b180, b181) beside it.
I assumed all three rest on the red 2x4 roof plate (b164). The picture does not show it exactly.
Page 60, step 19: two more clear 1x2 plates (b182, b183) go on the roof's red 2x4 plate (b164), on the free side of the red 2x2 brick. Only one is shown by arrows, but the parts box says 2x.
The parts list has 4 clear 1x2 plates in total, which fits two on page 59 and two here.

Page 61, step 20: two more dark green curved 2x2 bricks go on the upper roof, over the clear plates, one on each side of the red 2x2 brick. That makes six curved 2x2 bricks in total, matching the parts list.
I assumed b184 sits on the first pair of clear plates (b180, b181) and b185 on the second pair (b182, b183).

Page 62: the passenger car is coupled to the back of the wagon. The towball on the passenger car's black 1x4 plate (b143) snaps into the socket plate at the rear of the wagon (b75). No new pieces. The locomotive, wagon and passenger car now form a train.

Page 63 starts the last sub-model, a Christmas tree scene with a signpost. Step 1: a white round 4x4 plate (b186) is the base. Step 2: a white cheese slope (b187) goes on the plate, near the edge, as a snow bank.
The slope's stud on the plate is not named because the picture does not show which one.

Page 64, step 3: a reddish-brown round 2x2 brick (b188) is the tree trunk, on the white round plate. Step 4: a second white cheese slope (b189) and a red round 1x1 brick (b190) go on the plate beside the trunk.

The parts list has only one reddish-brown lego-3941. I used it here as the trunk, which is clearly a 2x2 round brick, and also for b53 on page 22. The page 22 piece may be a different part, for example a Pearl Gold or reddish-brown round plate. This is unresolved.
The picture does not show which studs of the base plate each piece uses.

Page 65, step 5: a small pink gift and a green flower with a white round plate on top are added to the white base plate (b186) beside the trunk. The gift is a pink plate, a black plate (the ribbon) and a pink tile on top, built in steps 1 and 2.
The picture does not show which studs of the base plate each piece uses, so those ports are not named.
Page 66, step 6: a black 6L bar (b196) is pushed into the open stud of the red round brick (b190) as the signpost pole.

Page 67, step 7: this builds the signpost sign. A tan jumper plate sits on a tan tooth plate (the pointed end) and a tan clip plate (step 1). A white spiral round tile goes on the jumper's stud (step 2). The clip then clips onto the black pole (b196).
I assumed the jumper's two anti-stud sockets fit over the tooth plate and clip plate studs. The picture is small, so which socket goes on which is a guess.
Page 68, step 8: the green pine tree (b201) is pressed onto the trunk, the reddish-brown round brick (b188). This finishes the tree scene.
Page 69 shows the finished model: the locomotive, wagon and passenger car coupled together, with the separate tree and signpost scene beside them. There are no building steps, so nothing is added.
Page 72 is the back cover, a product feedback advertisement. It has no building steps, so nothing is added.

Pages 3 to 13 gave their stacking only in notes, so the locomotive pieces b1 to b30 had no edges. That caused the many separate groups. These are the missing joined edges for them, taken from my stacking notes on those pages.
With these edges the locomotive body, the tender and boiler sub-assembly, the wagon and the passenger car are all connected. They are chained by the towball couplings: b80 to b14, then b143 to b75.

The tree and signpost scene (b186 to b201) is a separate model with its own base plate. The booklet builds it apart and shows it standing beside the train on page 69, so it is not joined to the train. This is the one expected separate group.
The stacking in these edges (for example which arch each wheel holder sits on) is my best reading of small pictures, as noted on those pages.

The two remaining groups are not a real problem. The train (locomotive, wagon and passenger car, all coupled by towballs) is one group. The tree and signpost scene (b186 to b201) is the other. The booklet builds the tree scene as its own model on its own white base plate (pages 63 to 68). Page 69 shows it standing next to the train, not attached to it. No joint or fastening between them exists in the booklet, so I left them as two separate groups and added nothing.

notes: Page 2 is a generic introduction (open the box, sort the bricks) with no building steps, so no pieces or joins were added.
Page 3, step 1: white 2x8 plate is the base (first piece, rests on nothing).
Step 2: red 2x4 studded wheel arch is placed on one end of the plate. Its bottom clutches the plate.
Page 4, step 3: a red 1x4 plate has a red 1x1 plate added, then the 1x4 is placed on the studs of the red wheel arch (b2).
The callout shows only one 1x1 plate, on the left end of the 1x4. The parts box says 2x, so I put the second 1x1 on the other end of the 1x4. This is a guess.
I assumed the 1x4 plate rests only on the wheel arch and not on the white base plate.
Page 5, step 4: two more red wheel arches are added next to the first, so three arches sit in a row.
The three arches are 12 studs long but the white base plate is only 8 long, so the arches must be staggered or overlapping. The picture does not show clearly which pieces each new arch clutches.
I assumed b6 rests on the white plate (b1) and the red 1x4 plate (b3), and b7 rests on the white plate (b1).
Page 6, step 5: three black 2x2 wheel-holder plates are placed on the three red arches. A dark green 1x2 plate goes between the first and second holder.
I assumed b8 sits on b2, b9 on b6 and b10 on b7. The picture does not show which arch is leftmost.
I assumed the green 1x2 plate (b11) rests on b2 and b6, the two arches it sits between.
Page 7, step 6: the model is flipped over. A white 1x2 plate is pressed onto two red studs at the end of the model.
I assumed those two studs belong to the end arch, b7, so b12 rests on b7. The picture does not show which arch it is.
Page 8, step 7: a dark green 1x2 plate and a black 2x2 towball-socket plate are added at the end of the model, side by side.

The picture does not show exactly which pieces each one clutches. I assumed the green plate rests on the end arch (b7) and the white 1x2 plate (b12), which it appears to cover. I assumed the black socket plate rests on b7.
Page 9, step 8: two gold side-handle 1x2 plates and two gold 1x1 plates go on either side of the green and black pieces at the end of the model.
The pieces look tan or gold in the picture. I took them as Pearl Gold from the parts list, which has 2x lego-48336 and 6x Pearl Gold 1x1 plates.
I assumed all four pieces rest on the end arch (b7). The picture does not show which pieces each one clutches.
Page 10, step 9: a red 4x4 plate covers the white base plate and the red arch studs on the open end of the model.
I assumed it rests on the white plate (b1), the arches b2 and b6, and the red 1x4 plate (b3). The picture does not show exactly which pieces it clutches.
Page 11, step 10: a red 2x4 plate and a red 1x4 plate cover the green, black and gold pieces next to the red 4x4 plate. The gold handles and the black socket stay visible.
The picture does not show exactly which pieces each plate clutches. I assumed the 2x4 (b20) rests on b13, b14 and b7. I assumed the 1x4 (b21) rests on b7 and the 4x4 plate (b19).
Page 12, step 11: a white 2x3 plate goes on the red 4x4 plate (b19), on the end away from the gold handles.
I assumed it rests only on b19, because the picture does not show it overlapping the 2x4 plate.

Page 13, step 12: four red clip tiles are pressed onto the red 4x4 plate (b19) around the white 2x3 plate, at its corners. Four plain red 1x1 grooved tiles go on the studs of the white 2x3 plate (b22).
The picture shows only one tile being added by arrow, but the parts box says 4x. I assumed the four tiles go on four of the six white studs.
The clip tiles are placed on the 4x4 plate. I did not add clip joins because no bars are involved yet.
Page 14, step 13: this is a separate sub-assembly, the locomotive front, and is not yet attached to the main model.

Step 1 is a red bracket (b31). Step 2 puts a black inverted bracket (b32) on its face, with a clear round tile at each upper corner and black round plates at the lower corners. Step 3 adds two black grille slopes (b39, b40) and another black round plate, shown by the arrow.

The picture does not show exactly which stud each small piece sits on. I assumed the four black round plates and both clear tiles are on the red bracket, and the grille slopes are on the black bracket. Ports are left null where unclear.
The output schema has no rests_on field, so stacking is given as joined edges. Pages 3 to 13 gave their stacking in notes only. They have no edges yet.
Page 15: the front sub-assembly from page 14 (red bracket b31 with grille and lamps) is pushed onto the front end of the main body. No new pieces.
The picture does not show which stud it clutches. I assumed the bracket's 1x2 plate clutches the exposed front studs of the white base plate (b1).
Page 16, step 14: a white 2x3 plate goes on the rear plates, and two dark green 1x4 grooved tiles go side by side on the red 4x4 plate (the boiler top).
I assumed the white plate (b41) rests on the red 2x4 (b20) and red 1x4 (b21) plates, and both green tiles rest on the red 4x4 plate (b19).

The clip tiles and 1x1 tiles from page 13 are not visible in this view. I assumed they are on the side not shown, or are meant to be replaced here, and I did not remove them from the graph. This is unclear.

Page 17, step 15: this is built 2x. Each copy is a small stack on the white 2x3 plate (b41): white round plate, red round plate (step 1), pearl gold round plate, then white round brick on top (step 2). They form the two chimney or dome stacks.
I identified the four pieces in the parts box as white 6141, red 6141, pearl gold 6141 and white 3062b. The box shows them as white, red and tan or gold round plates plus a taller white round brick.
The picture does not show exactly which studs of b41 the two stacks use. I assumed stud.1.1 for the first and stud.2.3 for the second.
Page 18, step 16: built 2x. Each copy is a red 1x2x2 window with a clear glass pane inserted, placed on the white 2x3 plate (b41) next to the chimney stacks.
The picture does not show which studs of b41 are used. The two stacks use stud.1.1 and stud.2.3, so I assumed the windows use stud.2.1/2.2 and stud.1.2/1.3 to fill the six studs.
Page 19, step 17: two gold 4L bars (handrails) are clipped along the two sides of the boiler.

Each bar is held by the two red clip tiles from page 13 on its side and by one gold side-handle plate. I assumed b23 and b24 are on one side and b25 and b26 on the other. The picture does not show which clip tile is on which side.
I used clip.1 of each side-handle plate (b15, b16).
Page 20 starts a new sub-model, the tender or coal car. The locomotive from pages 3 to 19 is finished.
Step 1: two red 2x2 round bricks with axle hole are stacked (b46, b47).
Step 2: a red inverted bracket 1x2 - 1x2 (b48) and a red 1x2 plate (b49) go on the top round brick. The bracket sits on one pair of studs and the plate goes on the other pair.
The bracket piece in the parts box is hard to identify. I took it as the red lego-99780 from the parts list.
Page 21, step 3: a red round 2x2 plate with axle hole (b50) goes on the red bracket (b48) and red 1x2 plate (b49).

Step 4: a dark green round 2x2 plate with axle hole (b51) goes on b50, then a white round 2x2 jumper plate with centre stud (b52) goes on top. The white piece is taken as lego-18674 from the parts list, since it is the only white round 2x2 plate there.

Page 22, step 5: a reddish-brown round piece goes on the white jumper plate (b52), then a clear round 1x1 tile goes on top. I took the brown piece as the reddish-brown lego-3941 round 2x2 brick, which is the only reddish-brown piece it can be. It looks flatter in the picture.

Step 6: a black wheel-holder plate (b55) is pushed up onto the underside of the bottom red round brick (b46). I took it as lego-4600, since the other black 2x2 pieces in the parts list look different. The picture is small, so this is a guess.
The clear tile might also be 3062b-based. I used lego-98138 Trans-Clear, which has 3 in the parts list.
Page 23: step 7 turns the round tower assembly on its side. Step 18 of the main model fits it onto the locomotive as the boiler, with its black plate (b55) pressed onto the body. No new pieces.
I assumed the black plate clutches the open studs of the red 4x4 plate (b19). The picture is small and does not show which plate it clutches.

Page 24, step 19: a red 4x4 plate goes on top as the cab roof. It sits on the two red windows (cab1.win, cab2.win) and the two white round bricks at the tops of the chimney stacks (stack1.top, stack2.top).
The model is also turned upright on this page. This adds no pieces.
Page 25, step 20: two dark green curved 2x4 bricks (b57, b58) are placed side by side on the red 4x4 roof plate (b56) to make the curved cab roof.

Page 26, step 21: this builds the chimney. A red round open-stud brick goes on a red jumper plate, a tan cone goes on top with its bar in the open stud, and white ice cream scoops (the smoke) go on the cone. The chimney is then pressed onto the front of the boiler.

The small tan piece in step 2 looks like a short cap. I identified it as the tan lego-11610 ice cream cone, the only tan round part in the parts list that fits. The scoops have no catalogue ports, so their joint to the cone's stud has no port.
I assumed the chimney's jumper plate clutches the two black studs of the black wheel-holder plate (b55) visible on the boiler front. The picture does not show this clearly.

Page 27, step 22: six black wheels are fitted to the wheel holders of the three black 2x2 wheel-holder plates (b8, b9, b10) under the locomotive, two wheels per plate. The red arrow shows one wheel going on.
The wheels are modelled as turning freely (revolute), clipped into the wheel holders. The wheel-to-holder port pairing is by convention, since the catalogue has no pin port for the wheel.
Page 28 starts a new sub-model, a green and red car (the coal or gift wagon). The locomotive is finished.

Step 1: a white plate (b69) is the base. The picture of this plate shows about 6 studs per row, so I took it as lego-3795 (2x6). The parts list has 2x 3795 white but only 1x 3034 white, and the 3034 was used for the locomotive base on page 3.
Step 2: a red 2x4 wheel arch (b70) goes on one end of the base plate.
Page 29, step 3: a dark green 2x4 plate (b71) and a second red wheel arch (b72) are added, so the two arches sit at the ends with the green plate between them.
Step 4: the model is flipped, and two red 1x2 plates (b73, b74) go on the studs of the green plate in the middle.
I assumed the green plate sits on the white base plate (b69) and touches both arches. The picture does not show the exact stacking.
Page 30, step 5: a black 2x2 towball-socket plate (b75) and two gold 1x1 plates (b76, b77) go on the end arch (b72). The gold plates sit on either side of the socket plate.
The gold plates look tan or gold in the picture. I took them as Pearl Gold from the parts list.
I assumed all three pieces rest on b72 only. The picture does not show exactly which studs they use.

Page 31, step 6: a black 1x4 towball plate (b80) goes on the arch (b70) at the open end of the model. Two red 1x4 plates (b78, b79) go on the red arch studs next to the white plate. The arrows show them on the studs beside the white plate.
The picture does not show exactly which studs each piece uses. I assumed b78 and b80 rest on b70 and b79 rests on b72.

Page 32, step 7: two red 1x6 plates and two red 1x2 plates are added along the long sides of the model. Only one 1x6 is shown with arrows, but the parts box says 2x. I assumed the second 1x6 and the 1x2 plates go on the opposite side or in the gaps.

The arrows on the 1x6 plate point to the black towball plate end (b80) and the gold plate (b76) at the other end. So b81 rests on b80, b76 and the red 1x4 plate b78. The mirror side b82 rests on b77, b79 and b72.
The two 1x2 plates (b83, b84) are placed on the arches b70 and b72 as a guess. The picture does not show them clearly.
Page 33, step 8: two white 1x2 plates and four white round 1x1 plates are placed on the red 1x6 side plates at the ends of the model, to look like a white trim.
I assumed one 1x2 plate and two round plates on each side. The first side is on b81 and the second on b82. The picture does not show exactly which studs each uses.

Page 34, step 9: two red 1x2x1 panels go on the white 1x2 plates (b85, b86), and four red round plates go on the four white round plates (b87 to b90). One round plate is shown by an arrow and the parts box says 4x.
I assumed each panel is on its own white 1x2 plate and each red round plate is on its own white round plate. The pairing of round plates is a guess.
Page 35, step 10: four gold round plates go on the four red round plates at the corners. Two dark green curved 1x4 bricks lie in the wagon bed.
I assumed each curved brick sits on one of the red 1x4 plates (b78, b79). The picture does not show which studs they clutch.
Page 36, step 11: the model is flipped. Two black wheel-holder plates with two wheels each are built, and one is pressed onto each wheel arch, b70 and b72, on the underside.
I assumed b103 goes on b70 and b104 on b72. The picture does not label which arch is which.

Page 37, step 12: two small gift boxes are built. The lime box is a lime plate, a black plate and a lime tile. The orange box is an orange plate, a black plate and an orange tile (the ribbon is the black layer).
Step 1 shows the lime plate with the black plate, step 2 shows both finished boxes. The lime box is shown placed between the green curved bricks in the wagon bed.
The picture shows only the lime box placed. I assumed the orange one goes in the same bed. I put the lime box on b73 and the orange box on b74, the two red 1x2 plates in the bed.

Page 38, step 13: this builds a candy cane. Six round 1x1 plates are stacked from the bottom up as red, green, white, red, green, white. A red curved brick (the hook) goes on the white plate at the top, and a red 1x1 tile goes on the stud at the end of the hook.
Steps 1 and 2 build the stack, and step 3 adds the hook and tile.
The catalogue lists no stud on the curved brick lego-6091, but the picture shows the tile pressed onto its end. I joined the tile to the curved brick with no port named.
Page 39: the candy cane from page 38 is pressed onto a free stud in the wagon bed, next to the lime gift. No new pieces.
I assumed it clutches the free stud of the red 1x2 plate b74. The orange gift is not visible in this view, so its position is still uncertain.

Page 40, step 14: two sweets are added. First, a pink swirl round plate goes on a lavender flower plate, and the flower goes on a free stud in the wagon bed. Second, a white round tile with a red spiral print goes on the stud of a white signal paddle, which makes a lollipop leaning on the wagon side.
The parts box shows a beige tile. I took it as the white lego-98138pr0013 spiral tile, because it is the one in the picture with a spiral and the catalogue has no other spiral tile.
I assumed the flower goes on the free stud of b73. The lollipop's stick rests against the wagon side next to the panel b92, so I used a contact edge. The picture does not show it clipped to anything.

Page 41, step 15: an ice cream cone with a chocolate scoop and two cookies are added to the wagon bed. The cone is a tan cone with a reddish-brown swirl plate on top. The cookies are the two cookie-print round tiles.

The parts list has only one lego-11610 tan cone, and I used it for the chimney on page 26 (b61). On page 26 the small tan piece may actually have been a Pearl Gold round plate. If so, b61 should be a lego-6141 Pearl Gold plate and the chimney scoops should sit on it. This page uses the cone for the ice cream, so the chimney part on page 26 is probably wrong.
The picture does not show exactly where the cone and cookies sit, so I used contact edges to the green curved bricks (b101, b102) instead of studs.
Page 42: the wagon is coupled to the locomotive. The towball on the wagon's black 1x4 plate (b80) snaps into the towball socket plate at the rear of the locomotive (b14). No new pieces.

Page 43 starts a new sub-model, the passenger car. Step 1: a white 2x8 plate (b131) is the base. The picture shows 8 studs per row, so I used lego-3034, the only 2x8 white plate in the parts list. The list has only one, and I used it for the locomotive base (b1) on page 3. That earlier plate was probably the lego-3795 2x6, so b1 may be the wrong type.
Step 2: two dark green 1x2 plates (b132, b133) go across the two ends of the base plate.
Page 44, step 3: a dark green 2x4 plate (b134) goes in the middle of the base plate, and two red wheel arches (b135, b136) go either side of it. The arches sit at the ends of the car.
I assumed each arch rests on the base plate, the green 2x4 plate and its own end green 1x2 plate. The picture does not show exact studs.

Page 45, step 4: the model is flipped, and two red 1x2 plates (b137, b138) go on the exposed studs of the dark green 2x4 plate (b134) in the middle. Only one is shown with arrows, but the parts box says 2x.

Page 46, step 5: a black towball-socket plate (b142) goes on the arch at one end. Two red 1x6 plates (b140, b141) go along the two long sides, one per side, and a red 1x2 plate (b139) goes at the other end. Only one 1x6 is shown with arrows, but the parts box says 2x.

The picture does not show exactly which studs each piece uses. I assumed the socket plate rests on b136, the 1x2 plate on b135, and each 1x6 plate on both arches and one of the red 1x2 plates (b137, b138).
Page 47, step 6: a black 1x4 towball plate (b143) goes on the end of the model opposite the socket plate. It sits across the end arch (b135) and the red 1x2 plate (b139).

Page 48, step 7: two red 1x2 plates (b144, b145) go on the exposed studs of the end arch (b136) beside the black socket plate (b142), one on each side. No arrows are shown. I assumed they rest on the end arch b136.

Page 49, step 8: this is built 2x. A gold 1x1 plate is pushed onto the underside of one end of a red 1x8 plate. Each 1x8 plate is then placed along one side of the car, over the red 1x6 plate and the red 1x2 plate on that side.

I assumed b146 sits on b140 and b144, and b147 sits on b141 and b145. The gold plates only hold the end of each 1x8, so they are joined only to their 1x8 plate. The picture does not show what else they touch.

Page 50, step 9: two gold lattice fences and two dark green 1x2 bricks go on the red 1x8 side plates. There is one fence and one brick on each side, with the brick at the other end of the plate from the fence.
I assumed b150 and b152 sit on b146, and b151 and b153 sit on b147. The picture does not show the exact studs.

Page 51, step 10: built 4x. Each copy is a small post of three round plates, white at the bottom, then red, then pearl gold on top. The four posts go at the four corners of the car's rim, on the red 1x8 side plates (b146, b147).
The picture does not show which stud each post uses. I assumed the end studs of each 1x8: stud 1 and stud 8 of b146, then stud 1 and stud 8 of b147.
Page 52, step 11: two clear 1x2 bricks (windows) go on the green 1x2 bricks, one per side. Four white round bricks cap the four corner posts built on page 51.
I assumed b154 sits on b152 and b155 on b153. Each round brick sits on the gold plate of one post, post1 to post4, in order. The picture does not show which post is which.
Page 53, step 12: two dark green 1x2 plates go on top of the clear 1x2 bricks (b154, b155), one per side.
Page 54, step 13: built 4x. Each copy is a red 1x2x2 window with a clear glass pane. Two windows go on each long side of the car, on the red 1x8 plates (b146, b147), between the corner posts.
The picture does not show exactly which studs of the 1x8 plates they use. I assumed studs 3 and 4 and studs 5 and 6 on each plate.
Page 55, step 14: two red 2x6 plates (b162, b163) make the roof, one over each long side. Each rests on its side's two windows and two white round bricks.

I assumed b162 covers the b146 side (windows pwin1 and pwin2, round bricks b156 and b157) and b163 covers the b147 side (windows pwin3 and pwin4, round bricks b158 and b159). This follows how I numbered the pieces on pages 51 to 54.
Page 56, step 15: a red 2x4 plate goes across the middle of the roof. Two white 1x2 plates and two dark green 1x2 plates go on the roof ends, giving the roof a raised lantern layout.

The picture does not show which plates sit where. I assumed the 2x4 spans both roof plates (b162, b163), and each white and green 1x2 plate rests on one of the roof plates: b165 and b167 on b162, b166 and b168 on b163.

Page 57, step 16: the car is flipped. Two black wheel-holder plates with two wheels each are built, and one is pressed onto each wheel arch, b135 and b136, on the underside. This is the same step as page 36.
I assumed b169 goes on b135 and b170 on b136.

Page 58, step 17: the car is turned upright. Four dark green curved 2x2 bricks make the curved roof, two at the ends and two in the middle. The picture shows the two end bricks already on and two arrows for the middle ones, which makes four in total.

The picture does not show exactly which studs each brick uses. I assumed b175 and b176 sit on the roof plates and green 1x2 plates at the ends (b162/b167, b163/b168), and b177 and b178 sit on the roof plates and white 1x2 plates in the middle (b162/b165, b163/b166).
Page 59, step 18: a red 2x2 brick (b179) goes on the roof, with two clear 1x2 plates (b180, b181) beside it.
I assumed all three rest on the red 2x4 roof plate (b164). The picture does not show it exactly.
Page 60, step 19: two more clear 1x2 plates (b182, b183) go on the roof's red 2x4 plate (b164), on the free side of the red 2x2 brick. Only one is shown by arrows, but the parts box says 2x.
The parts list has 4 clear 1x2 plates in total, which fits two on page 59 and two here.

Page 61, step 20: two more dark green curved 2x2 bricks go on the upper roof, over the clear plates, one on each side of the red 2x2 brick. That makes six curved 2x2 bricks in total, matching the parts list.
I assumed b184 sits on the first pair of clear plates (b180, b181) and b185 on the second pair (b182, b183).

Page 62: the passenger car is coupled to the back of the wagon. The towball on the passenger car's black 1x4 plate (b143) snaps into the socket plate at the rear of the wagon (b75). No new pieces. The locomotive, wagon and passenger car now form a train.

Page 63 starts the last sub-model, a Christmas tree scene with a signpost. Step 1: a white round 4x4 plate (b186) is the base. Step 2: a white cheese slope (b187) goes on the plate, near the edge, as a snow bank.
The slope's stud on the plate is not named because the picture does not show which one.

Page 64, step 3: a reddish-brown round 2x2 brick (b188) is the tree trunk, on the white round plate. Step 4: a second white cheese slope (b189) and a red round 1x1 brick (b190) go on the plate beside the trunk.

The parts list has only one reddish-brown lego-3941. I used it here as the trunk, which is clearly a 2x2 round brick, and also for b53 on page 22. The page 22 piece may be a different part, for example a Pearl Gold or reddish-brown round plate. This is unresolved.
The picture does not show which studs of the base plate each piece uses.

Page 65, step 5: a small pink gift and a green flower with a white round plate on top are added to the white base plate (b186) beside the trunk. The gift is a pink plate, a black plate (the ribbon) and a pink tile on top, built in steps 1 and 2.
The picture does not show which studs of the base plate each piece uses, so those ports are not named.
Page 66, step 6: a black 6L bar (b196) is pushed into the open stud of the red round brick (b190) as the signpost pole.

Page 67, step 7: this builds the signpost sign. A tan jumper plate sits on a tan tooth plate (the pointed end) and a tan clip plate (step 1). A white spiral round tile goes on the jumper's stud (step 2). The clip then clips onto the black pole (b196).
I assumed the jumper's two anti-stud sockets fit over the tooth plate and clip plate studs. The picture is small, so which socket goes on which is a guess.
Page 68, step 8: the green pine tree (b201) is pressed onto the trunk, the reddish-brown round brick (b188). This finishes the tree scene.
Page 69 shows the finished model: the locomotive, wagon and passenger car coupled together, with the separate tree and signpost scene beside them. There are no building steps, so nothing is added.
Page 72 is the back cover, a product feedback advertisement. It has no building steps, so nothing is added.
